identity.name: Colony of New South Wales
alt_names: Crown colony of New South Wales

land.text: New South Wales, which on 1 January 1901 'became a state' of the Commonwealth; the ACT and Jervis Bay were cut from it in 1911 and 1915

successors.note: Territorial evolution of Australia: 'On 1 January 1901, these colonies, excepting New Zealand (who chose not to join), became states'. The colony ends and the State of New South Wales is drawn by the commonwealth-of-australia dossier from the same day.

capitals.name: Sydney
capitals.note: The Sydney page says the fleet 'moved to the more suitable Port Jackson where a settlement was established at Sydney Cove on 26 January 1788' and that the colony was 'formally proclaimed by Governor Phillip on 7 February 1788'; it does not use the word capital for the colony (page silent), so Sydney as seat of government is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: Phillip's commission: 'The Colony of New South Wales was created as a penal colony'; it covered 'Australia east of 135 degrees east' and nearby Pacific islands (page also adds 'including most of New Zealand', which is not drawn here)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: legal jurisdiction, mainland and Tasmania east of 135 E plus Norfolk Island (transferred to Van Diemen's Land in 1844), about 3.47 M km2 by the gazetteer. The infobox of the colony page gives no area. Control on the ground was a few settled districts: Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire row draws only 7 cells (about 1,800 km2) of Australia in 1788, 53 cells in 1825 and 675 in 1850. The 1787 commission also nominally covered most of New Zealand; New Zealand is not drawn here (the United Tribes of New Zealand and later the Colony of New Zealand own it).

correction.text: 'New South Wales was extended west to 129 degrees east' (16 July 1825) and 'The southern islands of New South Wales were made the Colony of Van Diemen's Land' (3 December 1825)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: east of 129 E without Tasmania, about 4.79 M km2 (the largest the colony was). The same page says the Pacific-island boundary moved north to 39 12 S in July 1825 (a limit on the nominal New Zealand claim; not drawn). Macquarie Island (claimed 11 July 1810) stays in the colony to 1880 on the page's reading.

correction.text: South Australia was created 'between 132 degrees east and 141 degrees east, and south of 26 degrees south' (letters patent 19 February 1836, proclaimed 28 December 1836)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the colony without South Australia's original block, about 4.05 M km2; the 129 to 132 E strip south of 26 S and everything north of 26 S stay in the colony. Norfolk Island leaves on 26 September 1844 (no grid cell). New Zealand was attached to the colony by a boundary redefinition that 'arrived from London on 15 June 1839' (Colony of New Zealand page) until the separate colony took effect on 3 May 1841; it is drawn as the Colony of New Zealand from 1840. The paper 'Colony of North Australia' (17 February 1846 to 28 December 1847, the half of New South Wales north of 26 S) is not drawn: see notes.

correction.text: 'Victoria was created from the New South Wales territory south of the Murray River' (1 July 1851)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: about 3.86 M km2 without Victoria (modern Victoria used as the shape: the page names the Murray River, not a surveyed line).

correction.text: Queensland 'was made the Colony of Queensland' (6 June 1859 letters patent; formally separated 10 December 1859): what remains is New South Wales proper plus the land north of South Australia (129 E to 141 E) and the strip west of South Australia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: about 2.55 M km2. The Queensland page gives no boundary; the colony's 141 E western boundary is the page's own sentence 'Queensland's western boundary changed from longitude 141 E to 138 E' (1862). The NT block and the 138 to 141 E strip north of 26 S stay with New South Wales until 1862 and 1863.

correction.text: 'The portion of New South Wales west of South Australia was transferred to South Australia' (letters patent 10 October 1861)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: about 2.37 M km2; the strip between 129 E and South Australia's old western line of 132 E, south of 26 S, passes to South Australia.

correction.text: 'Land north of South Australia and east of 138 degrees east was transferred to Queensland' (13 March 1862)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: about 2.07 M km2; only the Northern Territory block (129 E to 138 E, north of 26 S) remains outside New South Wales proper.

correction.text: New South Wales proper, after 'The New South Wales region north of South Australia was transferred to South Australia' (6 July 1863), with the ACT and Jervis Bay (cut off in 1911 and 1915)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: about 0.68 M km2 by the gazetteer, the colony's final extent to 1900 (its last full year on the map). The two pages opened give no infobox area. Macquarie Island passes to Tasmania on 17 June 1880 (one cell); Lord Howe Island is below the grid.

region.text: Australia east of 135 E and the nearby Pacific islands (here Norfolk Island); the page's New Zealand clause is not drawn

ledger.note: 1788: Governor Phillip proclaims the Colony of New South Wales, all of eastern Australia east of 135 E. 'the First Fleet led by Captain Arthur Phillip founded the first British settlement' (18 January 1788); 'the Colony of New South Wales was formally proclaimed on 7 February 1788.' Land from the commission of 25 April 1787 on the Territorial evolution of Australia page: 'covered Australia east of 135 degrees east and nearby Pacific islands, including most of New Zealand'.

region.text: Macquarie Island was claimed for the UK and declared part of New South Wales

ledger.note: 1810: Macquarie Island is claimed for the United Kingdom and declared part of New South Wales (11 July 1810); one grid cell.

region.text: New South Wales was extended west to 129 degrees east: the strip of Australia between 129 E and the old 135 E line

ledger.note: 1825: the colony is extended west to 129 E. 'New South Wales was extended west to 129 degrees east' (16 July 1825), to include a trading post on Melville Island; the Pacific island boundary moved north to 39 12 S the same day.

region.text: the southern islands of New South Wales: Van Diemen's Land (Tasmania)

ledger.note: 1825: Van Diemen's Land becomes a separate colony. 'The southern islands of New South Wales were made the Colony of Van Diemen's Land' (3 December 1825); the Van Diemen's Land page: 'On 3 December 1825, he proclaimed the establishment of the independent colony'.

region.text: the territory between 132 E and 141 E and south of 26 S

ledger.note: 1836: South Australia is cut from the colony. South Australia was created 'between 132 degrees east and 141 degrees east, and south of 26 degrees south' (letters patent 19 February 1836) and 'proclaimed on 28 December 1836'; dated here to the proclamation, which is the South Australia dossier's founding date.

region.text: Norfolk Island was transferred from New South Wales to Van Diemen's Land

ledger.note: 1844: Norfolk Island is transferred to Van Diemen's Land (26 September 1844); no grid cell.

region.text: the New South Wales territory south of the Murray River, the former Port Phillip District

ledger.note: 1851: Victoria is cut from the colony. 'Victoria was created from the New South Wales territory south of the Murray River' (1 July 1851); the Colony of Victoria page gives the same date: 'independence from the Colony of New South Wales: 1 July 1851'.

region.text: northern New South Wales: the Colony of Queensland, 141 E western boundary (extended to 138 E in 1862)

ledger.note: 1859: Queensland is cut from the colony. 'On 6 June 1859, Queen Victoria signed Letters Patent to form the colony of Queensland'; 'A proclamation was read by George Bowen on 10 December 1859 whereupon Queensland was formally separated from New South Wales.' Dated to the proclamation, the Queensland dossier's founding date. The page gives no boundary; modern Queensland less the 138 to 141 E strip north of 26 S is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the portion of New South Wales west of South Australia

ledger.note: 1861: the land west of South Australia passes to South Australia. 'The portion of New South Wales west of South Australia was transferred to South Australia' by letters patent of 10 October 1861 (act of parliament 22 July 1861). The strip is read as 129 E to 132 E south of 26 S.

region.text: land north of South Australia and east of 138 degrees east, between 138 E and Queensland's old 141 E line

ledger.note: 1862: the land east of 138 E north of South Australia passes to Queensland (13 March 1862): 'Land north of South Australia and east of 138 degrees east was transferred to Queensland'; the Queensland page: 'Queensland's western boundary changed from longitude 141 E to 138 E'.

region.text: the New South Wales region north of South Australia, 129 E to 138 E: the Northern Territory

ledger.note: 1863: the Northern Territory passes to South Australia (6 July 1863): 'The New South Wales region north of South Australia was transferred to South Australia' (the Northern Territory).

region.text: Macquarie Island became part of Tasmania

ledger.note: 1880: Macquarie Island becomes part of Tasmania (17 June 1880); one grid cell.

region.text: New South Wales as it stood in 1900

ledger.note: 1901: the colony federates. 'On 1 January 1901, these colonies, excepting New Zealand (who chose not to join), became states' of the Commonwealth; the colony page: 'Federation of Australia, 1 January 1901, when the colony became a state of the Commonwealth.' The State of New South Wales is carried by the commonwealth-of-australia dossier.

wars.name: Hawkesbury and Nepean wars
belligerents: Indigenous Australians of the Hawkesbury and Nepean rivers
wars.outcome: The page: 'The first frontier war began in 1795 when encroaching British settlers established farms along the Hawkesbury River' and it 'ended the conflict by killing 14 Indigenous Australians in an ambush on their campsite' in 1816. No border moved on the page; the Indigenous side was stateless, so there is no contest zone.
wars.note: The page does not use the name 'Hawkesbury and Nepean wars' and gives 1795, not 1794, as the start.

wars.name: Bathurst War
wars.outcome: 'Governor Brisbane proclaimed martial law on 14 August 1824' in response to fighting with Wiradjuri warriors; no border changed.
wars.note: The page does not use the name 'Bathurst War'; the end date is not on the page.

certainty.note: Every colonial border here is a line in letters patent or an act (meridians 129, 132, 135, 138 and 141 E, the 26 S parallel, the Murray River), dated in the Territorial evolution of Australia page, so the lines are drawn sharp. They are legal jurisdiction, not control: the settled districts were a small part of the colony until the pastoral expansion, and interior lines were not surveyed on the ground for decades.

sources.title: Australian frontier wars

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. 6 pages opened for this dossier: Colony of New South Wales, Territorial evolution of Australia, Colony of Queensland, Colony of Victoria (cross-check), Sydney, Australian frontier wars.
MODEL. Cliopatria has no colony rows; its British Colonial Empire row draws only settled land (7 cells of Australia in 1788, 675 in 1850, 19,472 in 1880). This dossier and the five sister colonies draw legal jurisdiction from the letters patent, so together they partition Australia by dated lines (1788 east of 135 E; 129 E from 1825; Tasmania 1825; South Australia 1836; Victoria 1851; Queensland 1859; Northern Territory to South Australia 1863; Western Australia west of 129 E from 1829). The rendering agents should know the colony tint covers land the colony did not govern in practice; a gap-filler may prefer to draw the unsettled interior as nobody's land (rule 8). Decision for the orchestrator.
UNSETTLED. (1) The Colony of North Australia (17 February 1846 to 28 December 1847, proclaimed 16 January 1849) is left out of the ledger: a paper colony, shorter than ten years; the land is treated as still New South Wales. (2) New Zealand: the page's 1787 commission covers 'most of New Zealand' and the boundary was redefined to include it in 1839; the ledger does not draw it (colony-of-new-zealand starts 21 May 1840). The colony page gives 1 July 1841 as the separation date while the Colony of New Zealand page gives 3 May 1841. (3) Fort Dundas (Melville Island, 1824, 'as a part of the Colony of New South Wales') and Port Essington are single cells; not entered. (4) Norfolk Island's first settlement date is not on the pages opened. (5) The colony page's capital field is empty. (6) Claim to the 129 E to 135 E strip in 1825 is a bare meridian; the Western Australia dossier owns the land west of 129 E.
COUNTERPARTS. colony-of-tasmania, colony-of-south-australia, colony-of-victoria, colony-of-queensland, colony-of-new-south-wales are all written by oc-02-x; commonwealth-of-australia (oc-02-a) already lists the colony as predecessor.
